title: Let your AI send letters and postcards on pieterpost.com
pitch: From prompt to post. Your agent writes it. Send invoices, cancellation requests, heartfelt letters and birthday cards through WebMCP on pieterpost.com.
about_excerpt: From prompt to post. Your agent writes it. Send invoices, cancellation requests, heartfelt letters and birthday cards through WebMCP on pieterpost.com. Like Comment Story Updates PieterPost WebMCP, Because apparently the future comes with stamps Inspiration Most AI actions end on a screen. But invoices, cancellation requests, important documents, heartfelt letters and birthday cards still need to reach a real mailbox. PieterPost already turns digital messages into physical post. WebMCP gave us a way to let an AI agent use that complete service directly. What it does From prompt to post. Your agent can write and prepare a letter or postcard, then pay through Stripe’s agentic payments or create a secure payment link for you. After payment, PieterPost prints, stamps and mails it. Your agent can check the delivery status at any time. The person stays in control of the recipient, message and payment. The agent handles the work needed to send it. Without WebMCP, an agent could help write a letter, but the person still had to copy the text, open a website, complete forms, upload files and return later to check the order. PieterPost’s WebMCP tools connect these steps into one conversation. How we built it We added seven structured WebMCP tools to the existing PieterPost website: Upload a document or image Prepare a letter Prepare a postcard Create a payment link Check an order’s status Cancel a prepared order List orders from the current session The integration uses document.modelContext.registerTool() with strict input and output schemas. It also supports cancellation, safe retries, clear tool annotations and structured results that agents can understand. The tools use PieterPost’s existing website and fulfillment system. People can continue to use the normal interface, while compatible agents get a direct and reliable way to complete the same workflow. The complete browser-side WebMCP integration is available as an open-source MIT-licensed repository. Challenges Sending physical post has real consequences. We had to make sure an agent could not accidentally create duplicate orders or expose private letter and address information. We have a complex .pdf rendering pipeline to support all languages, emoji's and various formats for many countries around the world. Preparing an order does not send it. Payment remains a clear approval step. Stable operation keys protect against duplicate actions, and status responses contain only the information the agent needs. We also had to turn a multi-step physical service into tools that are simple enough for an agent to use without losing the safeguards expected from a real checkout flow. What we learned WebMCP is most useful when it removes the need for an agent to guess how a website works. The agent does not need to click through forms or interpret page layouts. It receives clear tools with known inputs, outputs and limits. The person still controls important decisions, while the agent handles the operational steps. The demo For the demo, Codex used PieterPost’s WebMCP tools to send a real thank-you letter to Tibo at OpenAI. Codex wrote the letter, prepared the order and created the Stripe payment link. After payment, Codex checked the order status, and PieterPost printed and mailed the letter. The product demonstrated itself: an AI agent sent a physical letter through WebMCP. Apparently, the future comes with stamps.
